public_rationale: The forecast concerns funding after OpenAI collapses. That condition had not occurred on the available record. Current funding rounds, high valuations, or fundraising difficulties therefore cannot support or contradict the predicted post-collapse shutdown.
limitations: The valuation limb lacks a numerical threshold.
The speaker specifies no period over which financing would remain unavailable.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: After OpenAI collapses, AI startups will be unable to raise money for compute or justify large valuations.

statement.excerpt: You won’t be able to raise money for a startup to spend money on compute, nor will you be able to convince somebody that your LLM wrapper will change the world, nor will you be able to justify a massive valuation.

from_speaker: You won’t be able to raise money for a startup to spend money on compute
nor will you be able to convince somebody that your LLM wrapper will change the world
nor will you be able to justify a massive valuation
our_interpretation: The surrounding context makes OpenAI's collapse the antecedent.
The plain reading is a shutdown of outside funding for AI startups' compute and investor acceptance of large AI-startup valuations after that collapse.
Claims about persuading investors are tested through completed investments and their terms, rather than whether an investor literally believes a startup will change the world.
Massive has no numerical threshold. A completed compute-financing round can test the first limb without inventing a valuation threshold.
This is a sector-wide financing-availability prediction, not a specified company's financial amount.
criteria.support_condition: Following a documented OpenAI collapse, comprehensive funding records and investor or lender evidence establish the asserted inability of AI startups to obtain financing for compute and large valuations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Following a documented OpenAI collapse, a bona fide completed AI-startup financing for compute disproves the funding prohibition, or a completed investment at an unmistakably large valuation disproves the valuation prohibition.
